briefs.capability: Account for exact 0/1/x/z bit-time and transition evidence in small digital VCD captures.
briefs.user: RTL verification engineers reviewing a short simulation capture.
briefs.pain: A plot alone does not provide a reproducible unknown-state duration ledger across aliased signals.
briefs.expected: The example intentionally exits 1: bus unknown bit-time is 10 bit-ticks. Clock 0/1 durations are 10/5 ticks; bus 0/1/x durations are 10/10/10 bit-ticks. Aliases share one signal record.
briefs.contract: ASCII VCD with one timescale, module scopes and wire/reg/logic variables. Binary and scalar values; widths 1–256. Initial bits are x at tick zero. Initialization x-to-known counts as a value change; known scalar 0-to-1/1-to-0 counts as rising/falling evidence. Same-tick changes count but consume no duration. The last timestamp ends the interval unless --end-tick explicitly extends the final held values. Unknown bit-time includes x and z; all per-bit durations sum to width times end tick.
briefs.limits: 2 MiB, 250,000 tokens, 512 unique IDs, 2,000 names, 100,000 value events and scope depth 32. No real values, EVCD, FST, dump-on/off intervals, analog timing or power inference. This is a deliberately small capture parser, not a waveform viewer.
briefs.acceptance: Exact duration conservation, aliases, same-tick glitches, scalar edges and x/z propagation; reject undeclared identifiers, invalid widths, incomplete scopes and decreasing timestamps.
briefs.notes: GTKWave offers interactive waveform inspection and many more formats. vcdvcd exposes timestamps and alias references; WAL provides programmable waveform analysis. WAL issue 46 discusses large-capture memory; that is adjacent demand evidence, not a request for this tool or proof of an unresolved defect. Our bounded JSON accounting does not replace these systems.
briefs.alternatives: Use GTKWave, script vcdvcd, or write a WAL analysis.
briefs.overlap: The existing traceweave repository analyzes AI-agent JSONL traces. This project reads hardware Value Change Dump signal state and bit-time; it is not another JSONL trace formatter.

briefs.capability: Explain edge-connected triangle islands and edge defects in a bounded OBJ mesh.
briefs.user: CAD/export pipeline maintainers inspecting a triangulated OBJ before downstream processing.
briefs.pain: Disconnected parts, seam duplicates and orientation conflicts need attributable face/edge evidence rather than an unexplained pass/fail.
briefs.expected: The invented OBJ has two separate closed tetrahedral edge surfaces, eight faces and no reported edge defects; exit 0. Multiple closed islands alone are not an error.
briefs.contract: UTF-8 OBJ triangle faces only. Positive and relative negative indices are validated at the face declaration, including texture/normal references. Exact-coordinate welding always applies. --weld-decimals 0–9 adds half-even decimal-grid quantization, not a Euclidean distance tolerance. Degenerate and duplicate faces are reported and excluded before edge incidence and island grouping. Point-touch contacts remain separate edge islands and are reported. Metadata is counted; materials are never loaded.
briefs.limits: 2 MiB, 20,000 vertices and 30,000 triangle faces. Coordinates: zero or absolute magnitude 1e-12 through 1e9, bounded decimal precision. No polygons, freeform curves, repair, self-intersection detection, vertex-manifold certification, solid volume or printability guarantee. closed_edge_surface only means each retained component edge has incidence two; it is not a full watertightness claim. Area is approximate.
briefs.acceptance: Recover two closed islands, attribute boundary/nonmanifold/orientation/contact defects, validate interleaved relative indices and reject forward/zero references and unsupported polygons.
briefs.notes: Open3D already clusters connected triangles and computes manifold evidence. Trimesh already offers adjacency, splitting and watertightness operations; MeshLab offers a broad interactive processing workflow. Trimesh PR 2620 discusses interleaved OBJ relative indices. Our explicit small-file evidence report is a narrower interface, not an absent competitor feature.
briefs.alternatives: Open3D or Trimesh scripts, or interactive MeshLab filters.
briefs.overlap: No existing owned repository is a triangle OBJ topology inspector. Point-table, GIS and media index tools do not implement OBJ face incidence or coordinate welding.

briefs.capability: Decode one captured Modbus RTU register response against an explicit typed CSV map.
briefs.user: Controls engineers reviewing an offline serial capture with a device register map.
briefs.pain: A CRC-valid byte sequence still needs explicit address context, byte order, scale and coverage evidence.
briefs.expected: Exit 0, with temperature -10, status 0 and pressure 12.5. All four captured registers are covered.
briefs.contract: ASCII hexadecimal RTU response, expected unit 1–247 and function 3 or 4, and mandatory zero-based --start supplied from the request. The response does not carry its start address: context is caller asserted. Validate length, even byte count and CRC16/MODBUS; CRC is not authentication. CSV columns exactly name,address,type,order,scale,offset. u16/i16 use AB or BA; u32/i32/f32 use ABCD/BADC/CDAB/DCBA. Byte-order labels describe wire order relative to canonical ABCD. Scale and offset use exact decimal arithmetic; finite binary32 values retain their exact binary value before scaling.
briefs.limits: One frame of 5–256 bytes and at most 125 registers; CSV 64 KiB and 125 rows. No overlapping mapped spans, serial ports, TCP, polling, device writes, request capture pairing, authentication or device-specific register semantics. Exceptions, unmapped words, map rows outside the response and nonfinite floats produce valid exit-1 evidence. Exact numeric representation is not a claim about sensor measurement precision.
briefs.acceptance: Verify known CRC vectors, all byte orders, signed values, binary32 scaling, complete map coverage, CRC failure and valid exception/nonfinite/out-of-range findings.
briefs.notes: libmodbus and Pymodbus provide full client/server protocol implementations. Modpoll already supports CSV-based device configuration. The broad modbus query also returned telemetry and energy platforms; these are broader integrations, while the focused modbus library query placed libmodbus first. No capability-absence claim or device reliability comparison is made.
briefs.alternatives: Use libmodbus/Pymodbus protocol code or Modpoll with appropriate device configuration.
briefs.overlap: No existing owned project decodes RTU response frames or typed Modbus register maps. General CSV validation and packet text tools do not provide this protocol contract.

briefs.capability: Partition local CUE/WAVE source sample frames into track, recorded-pregap and unassigned intervals.
briefs.user: Audio archivists checking how a CUE sheet would divide an uncompressed disc image.
briefs.pain: A split plan should explain recorded gaps and account for every source frame before any encoder runs.
briefs.expected: The generator writes invented silence into a new directory. The plan exits 0 and covers [0,44100) track 1, [44100,88200) recorded pregap, and [88200,176400) track 2. Planning does not modify source files.
briefs.contract: UTF-8 CUE with quoted basename-only FILE WAVE, consecutive AUDIO tracks and INDEX 01 plus optional preceding INDEX 00. Actual little-endian RIFF/WAVE PCM or IEEE_FLOAT metadata determines sample rate, frame alignment, data bounds and byte offsets. CUE indices are 75 frames/second and must map to integer sample-frame boundaries exactly. A sample frame contains all channels. Intervals use exclusive ends and cover each source frame exactly once, including explicit unassigned leading audio findings. SHA256 identifies source bytes.
briefs.limits: CUE 64 KiB, 16 local files, 99 tracks, 64 MiB per WAVE/128 MiB aggregate. No symlinks or path traversal, compressed audio, RF64/RIFX/extensible WAVE, synthetic PREGAP/POSTGAP, extra indices, copying, transcoding, resampling, tags or audio quality assessment. Unknown RIFF chunks are counted. --make-example only creates a new directory and refuses overwrite.
briefs.acceptance: Prove exact contiguous frame coverage, explicit INDEX00 gaps and leading findings, stereo byte offsets, source-byte preservation, RIFF validation, and rejection of unrepresentable frame boundaries and unsafe paths.
briefs.notes: Flacon already extracts and tags tracks from disc images. FFcuesplitter supports broader audio formats and text encodings. split2flac is archived and its README points to a replacement; it is a historical alternative, not presented as maintained. Flacon cue.cpp already treats INDEX00 and INDEX01. Our read-only sample accounting intentionally omits splitting and compressed formats.
briefs.alternatives: Flacon or FFcuesplitter for actual extraction; inspect the CUE manually before choosing an encoder.
briefs.overlap: The existing medialoom repository catalogs media metadata. This tool reads CUE index semantics and actual RIFF binary data to construct a complete source-frame partition, rather than another catalog.

briefs.capability: Reconstruct per-ply clock differences from a bounded annotated PGN mainline without hiding missing evidence.
briefs.user: Chess study authors auditing recorded clock annotations in a short standard-start game.
briefs.pain: Missing annotations or an unexplained clock increase should not silently become zero thinking time.
briefs.expected: Exit 0 with elapsed milliseconds [3000,2000,3000,5000]; known totals are white 6000 and black 7000 under the stated increment convention.
briefs.contract: One UTF-8 PGN, mandatory simple integer TimeControl base+increment, standard initial position and alternating SAN-like mainline labels. Brace [%clk H:MM:SS[.fff]] annotations are exact milliseconds. Assumption: each annotation is after its move and that move’s increment, including the first captured move. elapsed = previous same-side clock + increment - current clock. Missing evidence invalidates the next same-side difference until a new baseline is captured. An increase exceeding increment is a finding with no elapsed value. Balanced variations, semicolon comments and NAGs do not contribute clock evidence; header/body result agreement is enforced.
briefs.limits: 128 KiB, 64 headers, 10,000 plies, variation depth 32, token length 64; base 1–86400 seconds and increment 0–3600. No multi-stage/delay controls, FEN starts, variants, multiple games or sub-millisecond clocks. Move labels are not checked for chess legality. No engine, cheating, flag, network lag or actual-thinking-time inference; totals cover only computed evidence.
briefs.acceptance: Reproduce increment arithmetic, fractional milliseconds, per-side missing-clock resynchronization, ignored variations, and reject duplicate/leading clocks, malformed controls, wrong move numbers and result conflicts.
briefs.notes: python-chess already supports PGN clock and elapsed annotations and legal move handling. Chesslib offers a broader Java chess model; mliebelt/pgn-parser produces a structured PGN representation. Their broader capabilities are not replaced. Our dependency-free evidence ledger has stricter bounded input and deliberately does not validate legal chess.
briefs.alternatives: Use python-chess clock accessors, Chesslib or pgn-parser and implement the desired accounting convention.
briefs.overlap: No existing owned chess/PGN project was found. Other timing tools handle different input domains and do not parse chess mainlines and per-side clock evidence.
